To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Leishmania parasite and T cells were found within glomerular lesions of dogs with VL glomerulopathies, but not in non-infected control animals; (ii) ICAM-1 adhesion molecule was expressed in the glomerular lesions, but P-selectin was not; and (iii) the expression of Ki-67 proliferation marker and TNF-α cytokine was lower in infected than in non-infested dogs.

(1) T cells and adhesion molecules may play a role in the pathogenesis of glomerulopathy in VL; (2) the presence of CD8+ T lymphocytes may be related to the presence of CD 4+ cells in glomerular lesions; (3) there is a correlation between the presence of Leishmania in cells and the presence of T cells in glomerulopathy; (4) there is an inverse correlation between apoptosis and the expression of TNF

(1) T cells are the major players in canine VL glomerulopathies, (2) adhesion molecules are involved in the process, (3) the disease is not associated with apoptosis, and (4) the proliferative pattern is the main one in dogs with VL glomerulitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pathogenic mechanisms of VL nephropathy in naturally infected dogs, which is of interest in the context of the study of human VL.
the study of immune complex glomerulopathy in dogs with VL from endemic areas.
the participation of T cells, adhesin molecules and parameters of cell proliferation and apoptosis in VL glomerulopathies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune response in the kidneys of infected dogs is complex, but not yet well understood.
in the present study the immunological mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of VL nephropathy are complex and not yet fully understood.
the pathogenesis of VL nephropathy in naturally infected dogs is not yet completely understood and further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms of glomerular damage in these animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the glomerulopathy of canine VL, the participation of immunoglobulins, complement and the role of T cells are not as clear as in human VL nephropathy, but adhesion molecules may play a significant role.
the presence of T cells and the expression of adhesion molecules are associated with glomerular damage and may be important in VL glomerulopathology.

in the present study we have shown a complex immunopathogenesis of VL glomulonephritis with no clear participation of IgG, IgA, IgM and C3b but a possible migration of CD8 and CD4 T cells into the kidneys, participation of adhesin molecules ICAM-1 e P-selectin and diminished apoptosis in the glomeruloneprhitis in VL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T cell and adhesion molecules are important elements in the pathogenesis of VL nephropathy.
the presence of T cells and the expression of ICMA-1 and P-selektin are not correlated with disease severity, but with the presence of Leishmania.
the presence of CD8+ T lymphocytes in the glomerular tuft in dogs with VL may be an important factor in determining the severity of glomerulopathy.
